7.stem: The student wants to emphasize a contrast between the findings of the two studies. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Both Study A and Study B were published in peer-reviewed journals, one surveying college students and the other adults in ten countries.
options.B: Study A, which surveyed 200 college students about their sleep habits, found that those sleeping 8 hours scored higher on memory tests.
options.C: Study B surveyed 5,000 adults across ten different countries, a far larger and more varied sample than the 200 college students of Study A.
options.D: Whereas Study A linked 8 hours of sleep to better memory scores, Study B found no connection between sleep duration and memory.

9.stem: The student wants to convey to a general reader why this innovation matters. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Normally the vaccine must be kept frozen at -20°C, a temperature that no ordinary refrigerator can reach and that many clinic freezers cannot hold steadily for long.
options.B: The new stabilizer is a sugar-based gel, and a vaccine mixed with it stays viable for six months at room temperature instead of having to be kept frozen at -20°C.
options.C: Keeping a vaccine frozen at -20°C requires costly equipment and an electricity supply that does not fail, which is what led the researchers to look for a stabilizer.
options.D: By keeping the vaccine stable at room temperature, the stabilizer could bring it to the roughly two-thirds of the world where reliable freezing is unavailable.

11.stem: The student wants to draw a single general conclusion supported by all three studies. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: In the 2020 study, nurses working night shifts scored lower on memory tests than the colleagues who worked the day shift on the same wards.
options.B: Across several different populations and tasks, adequate sleep was consistently associated with better memory performance.
options.C: A 2021 study found that a nap taken soon after learning improved later recall in older adults.
options.D: In the 2019 study, students who slept eight hours recalled 25 percent more words than students who had been kept awake the night before.

12.stem: The student wants to offer a cautious generalization that a skeptical reader would be likely to accept. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: A 2021 study of a call center found that remote workers handled 13% more calls than their in-office peers, a gain that can be expected to hold across most job types.
options.B: A 2023 study of two firms found no significant difference between remote and in-office workers, so the gains reported in the other studies are unlikely to be real.
options.C: Across several studies, remote work was associated with modest productivity gains in some settings, though the effects varied by job type.
options.D: Remote work makes employees more productive, as studies of four tech firms and of a call center have now established beyond reasonable dispute for any job.

22.stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in migration distance between the two butterfly species. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Both the monarch and the painted lady are counted among the insects that migrate the longest distances.
options.B: While the monarch migrates up to 3,000 miles annually, the painted lady travels as far as 9,000 miles.
options.C: The painted lady migrates between Europe and sub-Saharan Africa, covering as much as 9,000 miles.
options.D: Each year the monarch travels from Canada to central Mexico, a journey of up to 3,000 miles.

23.stem: The student wants to highlight a surprising disconnect between how alert the 6-hour sleepers felt and how they actually performed. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: On reaction-time tests, the 6-hour sleepers performed as poorly as people who had stayed awake for 24 hours straight.
options.B: Though the 6-hour sleepers rated themselves as alert as the 8-hour group, their reaction times were as slow as those of people kept awake for 24 hours.
options.C: The 8-hour sleepers maintained stable reaction times throughout the study.
options.D: The study followed 48 healthy adults over 14 nights.
